Continuation stems are `phase3-continue`, then `phase3-continue-02` onward in order; each owns only `tickets/` plus its numbered `tests/test_seeded_phase3_<nn>.py`, pins its exact emitted identities/edges/tier/budget, asserts every existing fence path is existing Context, names each new module's registry owner, checks predecessor-test closure, carries the shrinking unseeded suffix, and emits no successor with the terminal exit batch. Pause-boundary render and ownership clarification: `dispatch-pause-boundary` also hooks `squatch/drain.py` and `tests/test_drain.py`, because the bootstrap drain must observe pause before `_draw_retry` records a retry-cap draw. Repeated production attempts proved that activating CLI/daemon pause routing and merge admission holds in one ticket exceeds one independently provable boundary. The repaired chain is therefore `dispatch-pause-boundary` -> `pause-resume-activation` -> `admission-holds-activation`; `phase3-continue-09` waits transitively for both activation tickets. Pause activation fences daemon/control/CLI/drain plus the daemon pause and production-composition tests. Admission-holds activation separately fences `squatch/mergequeue.py`, `squatch/merge.py`, `squatch/__main__.py`, `tests/test_mergequeue.py`, `tests/test_merge.py`, and `tests/test_daemon_composition.py`: the CLI composition root shares the already-live inbox between the drain control factory and production pipeline factory, and no merge fallback may construct a second inbox. Because embedding `squatch/drain.py` would breach requisition headroom, it remains a fenced on-demand inspection exception for pause activation.
